documents.title: Doc 80 - DECISION - Car 22 - Alleged contact with Car 4
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 22 - Alleged contact with Car 4

details.fact: Car 4 (Stromsted) and Car 22 (Garfias) collided at Turn 2.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: No further action
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. The Stewards summoned and heard the Drivers and Team Representatives (documents 73 and 74). Car 22 (GAR) was attempting an inside pass of Car 4 (STR) at T1 and had properly established his rights to the corner since he was slightly ahead at the apex. GAR did not make a full exit at Turn 1 which leads directly into the second part of the chicane. This allowed STR to remain on track and maintain partial overlap with GAR approaching Turn 2. STR ran out of room at the apex of Turn 2 where the cars collided causing GAR to spin. Generally, in chicanes, the car that established its rights in the first corner has the rights to the entire segment; however, it remains possible for the car that lost the rights to the first corner to reestablish its rights in the second corner. Once GAR allowed STR to remain on track after Turn 1, STR was entitled to fight back at Turn 2, and he did. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determine that even though GAR had the initial rights to the chicane, under the circumstances, STR had the right to contest Turn 2. Even though GAR remained ahead on the outside of Turn 2, he could not reasonably expect STR to disappear and he could have allowed STR more racing room on the inside of Turn 2. Having lost the rights at T1, STR could have declined to push the position, and GAR, having allowed STR to remain on track, could have allowed him more room at Turn 2. The Stewards determine that neither driver is wholly or predominantly at fault for the collision. Given that both drivers could have taken steps to avoid the collision, the Stewards elect to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 78 - DECISION - Car 1 - Allegedly leaving the track without justifiable reason
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 1 - Allegedly leaving the track without justifiable reason

details.fact: Car 1 (Nael) left the track between Turns 1 and 2.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 27.3 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations – a driver may not deliberately leave the track without a justifiable reason.
details.decision: No Further Action
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the Driver and Team Representative (document 72). The driver of Car 1 (NAE) explained that he was on the first lap and was positioned on the right-hand side of the track approaching Turn 1. Car 20 (POW), which was ahead of NAE, locked a wheel under braking and cut across NAE’s nose approaching Turn 1. NAE was subsequently unable to negotiate the corner as intended due to reacting to POW’s lock-up. The Stewards accepted that NAE’s compromised entry was a justifiable reason for leaving the track. The Stewards further determined that NAE did not gain any lasting advantage from leaving the track. Taking all the circumstances into consideration, the Stewards decided that No Further Action was appropriate.

documents.title: Doc 77 - DECISION - Car 20 - Allegedly leaving the track without justifiable reason
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 20 - Allegedly leaving the track without justifiable reason

details.fact: Car 20 (Powell) went off track between Turns 1-2.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 27.3 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations - Car 20 allegedly left the track without justifiable reason.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 71). The driver of Car 20 (POW) explained that he experienced a lockup during braking on the approach to Turn 1 and that he carried too much speed into the corner which caused him to go off between Turns 1 and 2. The Stewards further note that POW rejoined safely and without gaining a lasting advantage. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that POW had a justifiable reason for leaving the track and elect to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 66 - DECISION - Car 10 - Alleged failure to engage set-up procedure when leaving grid for formation lap
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 10 - Alleged failure to engage set-up procedure when leaving grid for formation lap

details.fact: Car 10 (Kato) did not engage the required start set up procedure at the start of the Formation Lap for Feature Race 1
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 37.6 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: No further action
details.reason: The Stewards, having received a report from the Technical Delegate (document 60), summoned the Driver and Team Representative (Document 61) and heard them along with the Technical Delegate and the Promoter’s Formula 3 Technical Director. During the hearing, the Driver of Car 10 (KAT) explained, and the Technical Delegate confirmed, that KAT had successfully engaged the start set-up procedure before initially attempting to start the car. KAT experienced technical difficulties and was unable to start the car. The master power had to be reset before the car would start. The Technical Delegate confirmed that after the reset, KAT properly attempted to engage the start set-up procedure three times before the car was started. Nevertheless, the procedure was not successfully engaged. The F3 Technical Director confirmed that the issue was with the Car itself, and that it was not attributable to the Team. KAT commenced the formation lap without the start set-up procedure engaged. However, he was able to successfully engage it for the Race start as required by Article 37.9 of the Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determine that neither KAT nor his Team were responsible for the issue, and that KAT made all reasonable efforts to engage the start set-up procedure. Taking all the mitigating circumstances into consideration, the Stewards elect to take No Further Action.

documents.title: Doc 65 - DECISION - Car 21 - Allegedly leaving the track and gaining an advantage on Car 6
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 21 - Allegedly leaving the track and gaining an advantage on Car 6

details.fact: Car 21 (Wharton) was attempting an outside pass of Car 6 (DePalo) at Turn 5. Both cars left the track and re-joined in the same relative order.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: No further action.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence and GPS evidence. The Stewards summoned and heard the Drivers and Team Representatives (documents 56 and 57). Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determine that both cars left the track and re-joined in the same order. During the hearing it was clear that neither had any grievances with the other’s driving through the segment in question. Under the circumstances, the Stewards determine that both drivers made a similar mistake and that equity between them remained after they re-joined the track. Therefore, the Stewards elect to take no further action.

documents.title: Doc 64 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 29 - Failure to follow RD instructions - Escape road instructions
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 29 - Failure to follow RD instructions - Escape road instructions

details.fact: Car 29 (Lacorte) went off at Turn 5 and did not stay to the right of the yellow line before rejoining.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.i. of the International Sporting Code (failure to follow Item 25.1 of the Race Director’s Competition Notes).
details.decision: Reprimand given to the Driver of Car 29 (Lacorte). This is his second Driving Reprimand of the 2026 Season.
details.reason: The Stewards reviewed video evidence. They summoned and heard the Driver and Team Representative (document 55). Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that Car 29 (LAC) left the track at Turn 5 and rejoined without staying to the right of the yellow line as required by Item 25.1 of the Competition Notes. LAC explained that he had issues with the car and was on radio with the team about whether or not to retire the car after the lap. He indicated that he was distracted by the conversation and accepted that he could have done better to follow the Race Director’s instructions. Taking all the evidence into consideration, the Stewards considered this to be an infringement even though he rejoined the track safely and without gaining an advantage and therefore impose a reprimand.

documents.title: Doc 48 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 23 - Unsafe release into the path of Car 14
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 23 - Unsafe release into the path of Car 14

details.fact: During the reconnaissance laps Car 23 (Shin) was released from its pit position into the path of Car 14 (Yamakoshi).
details.infringement: Breach of Article 28.12.a of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations
details.decision: Warning to the Team
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. The Stewards summoned and heard the Drivers and Team Representatives (documents 44 and 45). Car 23 (SHI) was released from its pit position into path of Car 14 (YAM). The initial release of the car was perfectly reasonable; however SHI stopped for several seconds just after his car’s nose entered the fast lane. After a few moments SHI slowly entered the pit lane and YAM came to a complete stop to avoid him. During the hearing SHI explained that he had been experiencing clutch issues and that is why he stopped. Video showed his mechanic leaning over the cockpit to attend to him, and SHI then departing on his own. YAM explained that he could see the situation unfolding and that he had reasonable time to react. Nevertheless, the Stewards determine that once SHI stopped, the mechanic could have taken better steps to re-establish release control over the car. Under the circumstances, the Stewards determine that a warning to the team is appropriate for this pre-race infringement.

documents.title: Doc 47 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 15 - Leaving the track and gaining an advantage
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 15 - Leaving the track and gaining an advantage

details.fact: Car 15 (Deligny) left the track at Turn 5 and cut the inside of Turn 6 while defending against Car 25 (Nakamura) and re-joined retaining the position.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video & GPS evidence. The Stewards determined that Car 15 (EDE) left the track at Turn 5 while defending his position against Car 25 (NAK) and re-joined still in front. It is generally accepted that if a car leaves the track while defending a position and re-joins retaining the position, that it has gained an advantage. In this circumstance EDE would be expected to concede the position, which he did not. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determine that EDE gained a lasting advantage and elect to impose the standard penalty for such an infraction.

details.fact: Car 24 (McLaughlin) left the track between Turns 5 and 6 and did not follow the instructions set forth in the Competition Notes.

details.decision: Warning
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the Driver and Team Representative (Document 26). Car 24 (MCL) went off the track between Turns 5 and 6 before rejoining at Turn 6. Given his angle of departure from the track, the Stewards accept the fact that he did not stay to right of the yellow line as required by the Competition Notes. Drivers are reminded to use all reasonable efforts to rejoin in the area indicated by Item 25.1 of the Competition Notes.

documents.title: Doc 22 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 11 - Impeding of Car 14 in Practice
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 11 - Impeding of Car 14 in Practice

details.fact: Car 14 (Yamakoshi) was impeded by Car 11 (Gladysz) who was driving slowly on the racing line between Turns 5 and 6.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 31.6 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Warning given to the Driver of Car 11.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the Drivers and Team representatives (Documents 15 and 16). The Driver of Car 14 (YAM) explained that he was on a flying lap on the approach to Turn 5, with Car 11 (GLA) ahead of him. GLA explained that he was on the radio and did not realize that YAM was approaching until it was too late to take steps to avoid impeding him. He further explained that, considering the characteristics of Turns 5 and 6, he did not consider it appropriate to move off the racing line at that time. He subsequently gave way after Turn 6. During the hearing GLA acknowledged his mistake and apologised. The Stewards determine that GLA unnecessarily impeded Car 14 and elect to issue a Warning in accordance with the Penalty Guidelines and consistent with previous precedents for similar infringements during the Free Practice Session.

documents.title: Doc 21 - INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - Failure to follow RD instructions - Practice starts infringement
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - Failure to follow RD instructions - Practice starts infringement

details.fact: Car 6 (DePalo) did not follow the Race Director instructions - practice start performed with Car 7 (Colnaghi) directly in front of him on the grid.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code - failure to follow Competition Notes, Item 15.1.b).
details.decision: Warning
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document 17). DEP explained that he released the clutch when Car 7 (COL) first moved. Unfortunately, COL immediately stalled and became stationary. DEP then moved immediately into the center lane and passed COL. Item 15.1.b of the Competition Notes provides that, “Under no circumstances should a driver make a practice start if another car is still stationary ahead on the same side of the grid.” The stewards acknowledge that COL’s stall played a factor in the situation, that DEP tempered his practice start once he realized that COL had stalled and that the passing manouevre did not prove to be dangerous to any other cars. The Stewards determine that a practice start infringement occurred, but in light of the forgoing mitigating circumstances elect to issue a warning which is less than the standard penalty for such an infraction.
